Do EXACTLY this, nothing more:
1. Read .skippy/IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md and pick the FIRST unchecked '- [ ]' task.
2. Read ONLY the files that task names — their CONTENTS are ALREADY PROVIDED above in the TASK FILES section. Trust the task description; it contains the API details you need.
3. Implement that ONE task with direct edits (edit_text_file for existing files, write_text_file for new ones). Never use subagents. Start writing by your third action at the latest.
4. Verify deterministically: run the task's attached '- verify:' command if it has one, otherwise the exact test command the task names. The harness re-runs that command after your turn and REVERTS the checkbox if it fails — a checkmark you did not earn costs the loop and gets annotated in the plan.
5. Use edit_text_file on .skippy/IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md to change that task's '- [ ]' to '- [x]' ONLY if verification passed. Change NOTHING else on that line: the task TITLE is an identifier the harness matches byte-for-byte, so rewriting or expanding it makes the task unmatchable and the run stalls forever (2026-07-31: a title rewritten into a 1000-character command blob cost four loops). Never delete or edit a task's indented metadata lines (verify/files/verify-failed). If a task needs clarification, add a NEW indented 'note:' line under it — never touch the title.
6. Respond with a one-paragraph report that STARTS with exactly one status token: DONE (task finished, verification ran and passed) | DONE_WITH_CONCERNS <the concern> | NEEDS_CONTEXT <what is missing> | BLOCKED <why>. Then: which task, what changed, how verified.
7. If the task you just checked is the LAST unchecked one: before reporting, run the gate command (npm run verify) and fix what it reports. The harness runs the same gate immediately after your turn, so a failure found now costs nothing and a failure found later costs a whole loop.
You may respond with exactly DONE-ALL-CRITERIA-MET only when EVERY box in .skippy/IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md is already '- [x]' — never while any '- [ ]' remains; a false DONE claim is detected mechanically and wastes the loop.

1	# Goal
     2	
     3	Two related pieces: (a) record which EDIT FORMAT each model reliably
     4	produces, alongside the existing reliability fields; (b) add a tool that,
     5	after an edit, runs the project's linter/tests and returns a structured
     6	pass/fail plus failure payload for a continuation prompt.
     7	
     8	Edit-format choice is the single biggest lever on local-model editing
     9	reliability, and the lint/test loop turns prompt guidance into a closed loop.
    10	
    11	# Requirements
    12	
    13	- `inventory.schema.json`, in the `model` definition (which already has
    14	  `additionalProperties: true`):
    15	  - `editFormat`: enum `["whole","diff","diff-fenced","udiff"]`
    16	  - `editFormatReliability`: enum `["validated","unverified","unreliable"]`
    17	- Propagate both through `xx-stack/scripts/generate-registries.mjs` into the
    18	  generated registries.
    19	- Add the fields to a couple of models in `inventory.example.json` and
    20	  `inventory.json` as examples, defaulting to `unverified`. Do NOT claim
    21	  `validated` for a model nobody has measured — that is a state assertion
    22	  without evidence.
    23	- New tool `verify_edit` `{ cwd, lintCmd?, testCmd? }` →
    24	  `{ lint: {ok, output}, test: {ok, output} }`.
    25	- `verify_edit` MUST shell out through the existing execution-policy path
    26	  (`execution_policy.ts` / `validateExecRequest`). Do not bypass the policy
    27	  gate — that gate is the reason this server can run headless safely.
    28	- Truncate captured output to a sane named cap and surface the FAILING TAIL —
    29	  that is what a continuation prompt needs. Shape the output so it can feed
    30	  `supervisor_emit_continuation_prompt`.
    31	
    32	# Files
    33	
    34	- Edit: `inventory.schema.json`, `inventory.example.json`, `inventory.json`
    35	- Edit: `xx-stack/scripts/generate-registries.mjs`
    36	- New: `xx-stack/mcp-server/src/verify_edit_tools.ts` + matching `*.test.ts`
    37	- Edit: `xx-stack/mcp-server/src/index.ts` (register)
    38	# Ground rules for this repo (from its own TODO — non-negotiable)
    39	
    40	- New MCP tools register via `server.tool(name, description, zodSchema, handler)`
    41	  and are wired in `xx-stack/mcp-server/src/index.ts` through a
    42	  `registerXxxTools(server, deps)` function — see `routing_tools.ts` for the
    43	  canonical shape. Follow it; do not invent a second registration style.
    44	- Tests use the built-in `node:test` runner (see `reliability.test.ts`). Add a
    45	  `*.test.ts` beside new runtime files.
    46	- The MCP server is ESM (`"type": "module"`) — import local files WITH the `.js`
    47	  extension. Shared `xx-stack/scripts/*.js` helpers are CommonJS; ESM
    48	  entrypoints use `.mjs`.
    49	- After any change touching `inventory.json`/schema/registries: run
    50	  `npm run inventory:sync` then `npm run inventory:check` (CI fails on drift).
    51	- xx-stack is a HEADLESS, local-first MCP control plane. No GUI. Cloud stays
    52	  opt-in. `inventory.json` stays the single source of truth.
    53	- Final gate: `npm run verify` (layout + agents + drift + inventory + tests +
    54	  hermes). It is green on a clean checkout — keep it that way.
    55	
    56	# Rules carried from the Skippy side (earned the hard way)
    57	
    58	- SCOPE IS LAW: touch only the files this task names. Report anything else you
    59	  find; never fix it in passing.
    60	- A numeric limit or a security property needs an assertion against the REAL
    61	  artifact, not a fixture.
    62	- Verify commands must be quote-free shell and must be capable of FAILING if
    63	  the claim is false.
    64	# Acceptance criteria
    65	
    66	1. Schema accepts the new fields and REJECTS values outside the enums.
    67	2. `npm run inventory:sync` then `npm run inventory:check` clean — no drift.
    68	3. `verify_edit` returns ok=false with the failing tail when a command fails,
    69	   and goes through validateExecRequest (assert the policy path is used, not
    70	   just that the command ran).
    71	4. Output truncation asserted against a REAL oversized output, not a fixture.
    72	5. `npm run verify` green.
    73
